result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-021 (waitlist placement with computed position display) at commit 1cdfada, branch feature/WF02-REQ-021. Did not trust TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 report, the test report, or the requirement_status.yaml narrative as substitutes for my own re-derivation. 1. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-021.md in full against all 4 acceptance criteria (§8's AC-to-design-element map). Every AC maps to a concrete, non-deferred design element; §0/§6 name open questions and scoping resolutions explicitly rather than silently resolving them; §7 confirms no schema change (checked apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts myself: registrations already has event_id/admission/created_at/id and the partial index registrations_waitlist_order_idx, unchanged by this branch -- git diff master...HEAD --stat -- apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts apps/bot/drizzle produced zero output). 2. Re-ran npm run lint myself: 0 errors, 2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings (Footer.tsx:11, Nav.tsx:10) -- unrelated to this diff, both files untouched by it, matches TEST-RUNNER's report. Re-ran npm run build myself: apps/web (Next.js/Turbopack) compiled successfully; apps/bot (tsc -p tsconfig.json) clean, zero errors. 3. Stood up my own scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432), ran `npx drizzle-kit migrate` myself -- applied cleanly with zero new migration files, structurally confirming the 'no schema change' claim rather than trusting git diff alone. Ran `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` from repo root: 16 files / 178 tests passed, 0 failed -- matches TEST-RUNNER's report exactly. 4. Independent AC2 re-verification with my own fixture (own chapter/event/3 users, not reusing any prior script): seeded three waitlisted registrations P/Q/R with created_at at 0ms/1000ms/2000ms offsets via direct SQL. Called getWaitlistPosition myself: before-flip positions {P:1, Q:2, R:3}. Captured Q's updated_at, then flipped P's admission to 'withdrawn' via a raw SQL UPDATE (no application function, per the design's §0-stated test substitute for the not-yet-built withdraw feature). After-flip positions: {P:null, Q:1, R:2} -- Q's position correctly shifted 2->1 and R correctly re-derived 3->2. Re-read Q's updated_at: byte-for-byte identical (1788761028475 === 1788761028475), confirming no write touched the second row's own columns while its displayed position changed. This is a live, from-scratch re-derivation, not a copy of TEST-RUNNER's AC2a result. 5. Independent AC3 re-verification with my own grep (a broader pattern than either prior report's): `git grep -niE "waitlist.?position|waitlistPosition|position.*rank|rank.*position" -- apps/bot/src` returned only: getWaitlistPosition's own declaration/JSDoc and call sites (registration.ts, handlers/registration.ts), the local `waitlistPosition` variable (handler-scoped, never persisted), test file references, and the same pre-existing schema.ts:158/273 prose comments (REQ-011-era, affirmatively documenting the absence of a stored column) TEST-RUNNER's report already flagged as ISS-0018. No column, cache, or persisted field anywhere. Schema diff vs master confirmed empty (see #1). AC3 holds. 6. Sanity spot-check of the tie-break (AC2b): read getWaitlistPosition (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts:228-272) once more myself. The ahead-of filter is `eq(eventId) AND eq(admission,'waitlisted') AND (lt(createdAt, target.createdAt) OR (eq(createdAt, target.createdAt) AND lt(id, registrationId)))`. Since `id` is the table's uuid primary key (globally unique, fixed once assigned), this makes created_at-ascending/id-ascending a genuine total order over the waitlisted set for a given event -- no two rows can compare as tied under this predicate, so the position is deterministic regardless of query/scan order. This matches the design's §2.3 stated tie-break and is independently confirmed correct by re-reading the code, not by re-deriving the full REQ-021 rework history (the fixture-collision bug TEST-DESIGNER fixed was a test-spec mechanics issue, not a defect in this ordering logic). 7. Confirmed full requirement scope: git status --porcelain clean before and after all scratch work (my own scratch script apps/bot/scratch-rv-req021-ac2.ts was deleted, scratch Postgres torn down with `docker compose down -v` before this handoff). All design-doc-listed files present and touched exactly as §Files-this-design-expects states: apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts (+getWaitlistPosition), apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts (position wiring), apps/bot/src/i18n/types.ts/ru.ts/en.ts (two new keys each, grepped and confirmed present with matching copy in all three). git diff --stat master...HEAD shows exactly the files the design and prior gates describe, nothing stray. Grepped registration.ts/handlers/registration.ts/i18n files for TODO/FIXME/XXX: zero matches. 8. docs/agents/requirements.yaml's REQ-021 entry: description and all 4 acceptance_criteria match the implemented scope precisely (waitlisted admission + position display, computed-never-stored via updated_at-unchanged proof, git-grep-clean AC3, unbounded waitlist). status is still 'pending', which is correct and expected at this step -- DOC-UPDATER (Step 6) has not run yet, not staleness. 9. Judgment on the 6 filed issues, none blocking this release: - ISS-0013 (CI has no Postgres service, MAJOR, from REQ-019): still open, still correctly scoped as forward-looking test-infrastructure debt -- every verification in this run (mine included) executed real code against a real, locally-provisioned Postgres with real reported output. Not blocking, consistent with the REQ-019/REQ-020 release validations' reasoning. - ISS-0014 (DB-backed vitest files race under default per-file parallelism, MINOR): not applicable to my own re-runs since I always used --no-file-parallelism. Not blocking. - ISS-0015 (REQ-019 test-spec wording inconsistency, MINOR): scoped to REQ-019's own spec, not applicable to REQ-021 at all. - ISS-0016 (TEST-RUNNER inflated test count on REQ-019, MINOR): scoped to REQ-019's own report; REQ-021's TEST-RUNNER report (178) and my own independent re-run (178) agree exactly, no discrepancy here. - ISS-0017 (REQ-020 test-spec fixture defects, MINOR): scoped to REQ-020's own spec file, not applicable to REQ-021. - ISS-0018 (REQ-021 test-spec's AC3 grep list doesn't pre-account for the pre-existing schema.ts:158 comment match, MINOR): confirmed accurate -- I independently reproduced the identical false-positive grep hit (see #5) and confirmed by my own git diff check that schema.ts is untouched by this branch, so the match is structurally pre-existing and semantically supportive of AC3 rather than a violation of it. This is a test-spec wording precision issue only (spec's expected-match list should name a fifth accounted-for category), not an implementation defect -- correctly left for TEST-DESIGNER to fix at the source in a future pass. Non-blocking. Overall: every independent check I ran -- lint, build, full test suite from a cold DB with a fresh migration, an independently-constructed AC2 fixture with my own updated_at byte-comparison, an independently-run AC3 grep, and a fresh read of the tie-break ordering logic -- agrees with all four prior gates (REVIEWER, SECURITY-REVIEWER, TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, TEST-RUNNER). No half-implemented scope, no stray TODOs, clean git tree, all design-doc-listed files present.
